patient_answer: Measures blood sugar concentration after an overnight fast of 8 to 12 hours.
Normal fasting range: 70 to 99 mg/dL (3.9 to 5.5 mmol/L).
Diabetes threshold: 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher on two separate test occasions.
Plain drinking water is permitted during fasting; do not drink tea, coffee, milk, or juices.

doctor_answer.assessment: Diagnostic threshold for impaired fasting glucose and diabetes mellitus (LOINC: 1558-6: Fasting glucose in plasma).
doctor_answer.investigations: Fasting Plasma Glucose (FBS), HbA1c (LOINC: 4548-4), 75g 2-hour Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT), Lipid Profile.
doctor_answer.management: If FBS >= 126 mg/dL confirmed: initiate lifestyle modification (diet, exercise) and evaluate eligibility for Metformin per ADA Standards of Care.
references: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care in Diabetes

staff_answer: Verify patient fasting status (>=8 hours). Collect venous sample in sodium fluoride / potassium oxalate (grey-top tube) to prevent in vitro glycolysis.
red_flags: FBS > 300 mg/dL with ketones or altered sensorium (suspect DKA / HHS)
FBS < 60 mg/dL with neuroglycopenia (shakiness, diaphoresis - give 15g fast carbs)
follow_up_questions: How many hours did you fast before having your blood drawn?
Do you have family history of diabetes?
avoid: Do NOT exercise vigorously immediately before the blood draw
Do NOT chew gum or smoke during the fasting window
source: LOINC Standards (Regenstrief Institute) & ADA Standards of Care
